_about: Published classifications the Find your method tree can be viewed through, one at a time: one per side, the strongest we found (2026-11-17: Saunders et al. 2019, a textbook, and Grimes & Schulz 2002, clinical designs only, were dropped to keep the references few; their item-by-item mappings are in this file as of commit e628caa, and how each source was checked is in docs/method-tree-sources.md and docs/method-tree-taxonomies.md). question: schemes for the left side (what you study), mapping each kind of question (suit). tool: schemes for the right side (your tool), mapping each Method (design id). In each scheme, items maps an id to the group(s) it belongs to; basis says how: named (the source itself names it) or definition (we applied the source's own definition, see note). An id left out of items is not classified by that source, and the app shows it as such. The first scheme on each side is the game's own grouping, labelled as ours. How each source was checked: docs/method-tree-sources.md, docs/method-tree-taxonomies.md, docs/method-tree-mesh.md.

question.name: The game's suits
question.cite: Methodical's own nine kinds of question (the suits on the cards).

question.name: Gregor (2006)
question.what: Goals of theory: what a study's answer is for
question.cite: Gregor (2006). The Nature of Theory in Information Systems. MIS Quarterly 30(3), Table 2, p. 620.

groups.name: Explanation
groups.def: Says what is, how, why, when, and where.

groups.name: Prediction

DESCRIBE.note: Gregor's first goal is analysis and description.

EXPLORE.note: Describing what is going on, without testing causes.

MEASURE.note: Defining and describing the constructs themselves.

EXPLAIN.note: How and why, from a mechanism or theory.

tool.name: The game's families
tool.cite: Methodical's own nine Method families (the colours on the cards). Each says below which published category it follows, if any.

descriptive.cite: CDC (2012). Principles of Epidemiology in Public Health Practice, 3rd ed., lesson 1, section 6: descriptive epidemiology covers time, place and person.
descriptive.note: Cross-sectional studies are filed here: the same course calls them a perfectly fine tool for descriptive epidemiology (section 7).

analytical.cite: CDC (2012). Principles of Epidemiology in Public Health Practice, 3rd ed., lesson 1, section 7: the key feature of analytic epidemiology is a comparison group.

quasi.cite: Own grouping. The term follows the ERIC thesaurus descriptor "Quasiexperimental Design".
quasi.note: No family of its own in MeSH or EQUATOR.

experimental.cite: CDC (2012). Principles of Epidemiology in Public Health Practice, 3rd ed., lesson 1, section 7: in an experimental study the investigator determines the exposure.

qualitative.note: Mixed methods has no MeSH heading.

synthesis.cite: MeSH 2026: Evidence Synthesis (D000099290, publication type V03.500).
synthesis.note: MeSH files bibliometric methods (co-citation, coupling) under information science.

measurement.cite: MeSH 2026: Validation Study (D023361); otherwise the game's own grouping.

computational.cite: Own grouping: no published category groups models, simulation, prediction and cost-effectiveness.

engineering.cite: Own grouping, anchored in Hevner et al. (2004), design science, and Gregor (2006), design and action.

tool.name: MeSH 2026
tool.what: Study designs and methods in the U.S. National Library of Medicine's subject headings
tool.cite: U.S. National Library of Medicine. Medical Subject Headings (MeSH), 2026 edition, checked through the MeSH RDF API on 2026-11-17.
tool.rule: Each Method sits under the MeSH heading that names it, grouped by the MeSH tree; where MeSH has no heading for it, under the nearest broader one, or not classified.

case-report.note: Case Reports (D002363). Publication type for reports of individual cases.

cross-sectional.note: Cross-Sectional Studies (D003430). Own heading, under Epidemiologic Studies.

ecological.note: Epidemiologic Studies (D016021). No heading; 'ecological' appears only as Ecological Fallacy/Bias under Bias. Nearest is Epidemiologic Studies.

surveillance.note: Population Surveillance (D011159). Own heading, filed under Data Collection > Surveys and Questionnaires.

cohort-prospective.note: Prospective Studies (D011446). Own heading, under Cohort Studies.

cohort-retrospective.note: Retrospective Studies (D012189). Own heading, filed under both Case-Control and Cohort Studies.

case-control.note: Case-Control Studies (D016022). Own heading, under Epidemiologic Studies.

case-crossover.note: Epidemiologic Studies (D016021). No heading or entry term; nearest is Epidemiologic Studies.

target-trial.note: Observational Study (D064888). No heading; it analyses observational data, so nearest is the Observational Study publication type.

iv.note: Observational Study (D064888). No heading; 'Natural Experiment' is an entry term of Observational Study. Doubtful: IV is an analysis, not a design.

mendelian.note: Mendelian Randomization Analysis (D057182). Own heading, under Molecular Epidemiology.

gwas.note: Genome-Wide Association Study (D055106). Own heading, under Epidemiologic Research Design and Molecular Epidemiology.

case-cohort.note: Case-Control Studies (D016022). 'Nested Case-Control Studies' is an entry term of Case-Control Studies; case-cohort itself has no term.

did.note: Controlled Before-After Studies (D065187). Controlled Before-After Studies is the design that difference-in-differences analyses.

rdd.note: Non-Randomized Controlled Trials as Topic (D065228). No heading; 'Quasi-Experimental Studies' is an entry term of Non-Randomized Controlled Trials as Topic.

its.note: Interrupted Time Series Analysis (D065186). Own heading, under Epidemiologic Studies.

synthetic-control.note: Non-Randomized Controlled Trials as Topic (D065228). No heading; nearest is Non-Randomized Controlled Trials as Topic (entry term Quasi-Experimental Studies). Doubtful.

rct.note: Randomized Controlled Trial (D016449). Publication type, under Controlled Clinical Trial.

cluster-rct.note: Randomized Controlled Trial (D016449). No heading or entry term for cluster randomization; nearest is Randomized Controlled Trial.

crossover.note: Cross-Over Studies (D018592). Own heading, but MeSH files it under Epidemiologic Research Design, not under Clinical Trial.

n-of-1.note: Single-Case Studies as Topic (D000080907). 'N-of-1 Trials as Topic' is an entry term of Single-Case Studies as Topic, under Clinical Trials as Topic (E05).

stepped-wedge.note: Randomized Controlled Trial (D016449). No heading or entry term; nearest is Randomized Controlled Trial.

adaptive-platform.note: Adaptive Clinical Trial (D000076362). Own publication type; 'Platform Trial' is one of its entry terms.

grounded-theory.note: Grounded Theory (D066296). Own heading, under Empirical Research beside Qualitative Research.

interviews-thematic.note: Qualitative Research (D036301). No heading for thematic analysis; Interviews as Topic is a data-collection technique, so Qualitative Research.

mixed-sequential.note: Empirical Research (D036262). No heading or entry term for mixed methods; nearest heading covering both strands is Empirical Research.

systematic-review.note: Systematic Review (D000078182). Publication type under Evidence Synthesis; Meta-Analysis is its sibling.

scoping-review.note: Scoping Review (D000098583). Publication type under Evidence Synthesis.

network-meta.note: Network Meta-Analysis (D000099094). Only tree V03.600.001 under Meta-Analysis, which is also V03.500.004; grouped through that parent.

ipd-meta.note: Meta-Analysis (D017418). No heading for individual participant data; nearest is Meta-Analysis (V03.500.004).

umbrella-review.note: Systematic Review (D000078182). 'Umbrella Review' is an entry term of Systematic Review.

rapid-review.note: Evidence Synthesis (D000099290). No heading or entry term; nearest is Evidence Synthesis.

realist-review.note: Evidence Synthesis (D000099290). No heading or entry term; nearest is Evidence Synthesis.

prior-art.note: Evidence Synthesis (D000099290). No heading; Evidence Synthesis covers it only by its broad scope note. Doubtful.

multivocal-review.note: Evidence Synthesis (D000099290). No heading; Gray Literature is a topic, so nearest is Evidence Synthesis.

diagnostic-accuracy.note: Sensitivity and Specificity (D012680). No heading for the study design; Sensitivity and Specificity names the measures it estimates.

reliability.note: Reproducibility of Results (D015203). Own heading ('Test-Retest Reliability' is an entry term), under Epidemiologic Research Design.

validation.note: Validation Study (D023361). Validation Study publication type.

nomological.note: Validation Study (D023361). No heading for nomological networks or construct validity; nearest is Validation Study.

analytical-model.note: Models, Theoretical (D008962). Own heading; 'Mathematical Model' is an entry term.

simulation.note: Computer Simulation (D003198). Own heading, under Computing Methodologies.

prediction-model.note: Prediction Methods, Machine (D000098411). Prediction Methods, Machine; its label says machine, but its scope note covers statistical models too.

pilot.note: Pilot Projects (D010865). Own heading ('Pilot Study' is an entry term), under Epidemiologic Study Characteristics.

think-aloud.note: User-Centered Design (D000086825). 'Usability Testing' is an entry term of User-Centered Design, filed under Software.

reasoning._about: The approach to theory belongs to the research, not to the Method, so the tree asks it as part of your situation and each answer names its approach. Definitions: Timmermans & Tavory (2012, pp. 170–171), who set out the three logics side by side; the deciding question: whether explicit hypotheses exist to be tested (Suddaby 2006, p. 636) and whether what you observe surprises existing theory (Timmermans & Tavory 2012, p. 169). Each answer cites its own page (ref). groups: def and data are our words for those definitions. items: what published sources say about particular Methods (basis named: the source names the reasoning; definition: these definitions applied to how that source defines the Method, note says why). Shown only in a Method's details, as how the Method has been used; a Method left out is one no source we read settles. 2026-11-17: replaced Saunders et al. (2019), a textbook, at the user's request; how both were checked is in docs/method-tree-sources.md.
reasoning.name: Timmermans & Tavory (2012)
reasoning.what: Approaches to theory: deduction, induction and abduction
reasoning.cite: Timmermans & Tavory (2012). Theory construction in qualitative research: from grounded theory to abductive analysis. Sociological Theory 30(3), pp. 169–171.
reasoning.rule: The three work together: abduction forms a hypothesis, deduction works out what it implies, and induction tests it against the data.

groups.name: Deductive
groups.def: Start from a rule (a theory), apply it to a case, and predict a result that confirms or falsifies the rule.
groups.data: Collect data to test the hypothesis your theory implies.

groups.name: Inductive
groups.def: Start from many cases and infer the general rule they share.
groups.data: Collect data first, compare cases, and let the patterns suggest a rule.

groups.name: Abductive
groups.def: Start from a surprising observation and propose the explanation that would make it unsurprising.
groups.data: Use what existing theory cannot explain to form a new hypothesis, then test it with more data.

situation.q: Is there already a theory you want to test?
situation.help: Whether a theory exists, and whether what you see fits it, decides how your research uses theory. One study can combine approaches.

options.label: Yes, and I want to test it
options.hint: The theory gives you hypotheses; your data can confirm or falsify them.

options.label: No, there's no hypothesis to test yet
options.hint: With no explicit hypothesis to test, build theory from the data.

options.label: Yes, but what I see doesn't fit it
options.hint: A finding that surprises existing theory calls for a new explanation.

rct.note: Item 2b: hypotheses are pre-specified questions being tested.
rct.cite: Moher et al. (2010). CONSORT 2010 Explanation and Elaboration. BMJ.

ab-test.note: Section 1: the experiment retains or rejects the null hypothesis of no difference.
ab-test.cite: Kohavi, Henne & Sommerfield (2007). Practical guide to controlled experiments on the web. KDD.

nomological.note: The proposed interpretation generates specific testable hypotheses.
nomological.cite: Cronbach & Meehl (1955). Construct validity in psychological tests. Psychological Bulletin.

grounded-theory.note: Theory generated from data inductively; deduction and abduction also have a part as the theory develops.
grounded-theory.cite: Chun Tie, Birks & Francis (2019). Grounded theory research: a design framework for novice researchers. SAGE Open Medicine.

case-study.note: Findings can serve theory development and theory testing.
case-study.cite: Crowe et al. (2011). The case study approach. BMC Medical Research Methodology.

process-tracing.note: p. 824: evaluates prior hypotheses and discovers new ones.
process-tracing.cite: Collier (2011). Understanding Process Tracing. PS: Political Science & Politics.

interviews-thematic.note: p. 58: coding can be inductive, or deductive (theory-driven).
interviews-thematic.cite: Braun & Clarke (2012). Thematic analysis. APA Handbook of Research Methods in Psychology, vol. 2.

mixed-sequential.note: p. 17: mixed methods research uses induction, deduction and abduction. Said of mixed methods in general.
mixed-sequential.cite: Johnson & Onwuegbuzie (2004). Mixed Methods Research: A Research Paradigm Whose Time Has Come. Educational Researcher.

systematic-review.note: Reviews can generate or evaluate theories: theory building is inductive, theory testing deductive.
systematic-review.cite: Page et al. (2021). The PRISMA 2020 statement. BMJ.

realist-review.note: Builds theory-based explanations, then tests and refines them in turn: the cycle led by abduction (Timmermans & Tavory 2012, p. 171); the source does not use the word.
realist-review.cite: Wong et al. (2013). RAMESES publication standards: realist syntheses. BMC Medicine.

design-science.note: An iterated build-and-evaluate loop in which theories are applied, tested, modified and extended: the cycle led by abduction (Timmermans & Tavory 2012, p. 171).
design-science.cite: Hevner et al. (2004). Design science in information systems research. MIS Quarterly.
